title: Nonnegativity of stable influence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $i$ be a coordinate. For every $\\rho\\in[0,1]$, the stable influence of $f$ at parameter $\\rho$ and coordinate $i$ is nonnegative; here stable influence is the sum, over coordinate subsets containing $i$, of $\\rho^{|S|-1}$ times the square of the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
